facts.fact: E3 (negative control) is |mean(L_stat - F_stat)| < m; if L_stat is ahead, E1 is downgraded to 'more training helps'. Only the 'ahead' branch is written. There is no rule for L_stat behind F_stat by more than m, and no per-seed or sign conditions (the other hypotheses use the three-part rule (a)-(c)).
E3 is not run, has no pre-registered rule and no scorer code. 'Evolved' stays unlicensed until E3 runs.
Design prediction for E3: passes, about 60%.

Design text: 'a stationary nursery for the E3 control: one fixed table for the whole nursery, seeds 1-3, giving W0stat_s'; L_stat and F_stat run 'in the stationary world that matches their nursery'. The text does not say whether one table is shared by all three model seeds and all worlds, or one per model seed.

The table seed is tunable: section 6.7 lets smoke runs set 'the stationary nursery's table seed'. The critique asks to fix it now by a hash rule (for example hash32(nurserySeed, STAT, s)) and remove it from the tunable list.

Critique reading (not measured here): one fixed table seen in training means F_stat already holds that table, so extra training cannot show up, and E3 cannot detect the alternative it is meant to guard against.

Regime checks M1-M3 are stated for E1-E4: if one fails, E1-E4 read 'no test'. The design does not say how they apply in a stationary world, and the scorer computes the reference minds (O, T, S, RND) only on the seasonal preset.
m = 1.02 is v1a's margin (sd of F - F2 = 0.34). v1b reused it. No F2_stat run is in the plan, so a stationary floor cannot be computed unless one is added.
Readout window: from the first season boundary to the end of life. Code starts the window at log.seasons[1] ?? 0, so a life with no season boundary is read from tick 0 (a departure from the design).

Planned size: 48 F_stat and 48 L_stat life runs (model seeds 1-3 x world seeds 101-116), plus 3 stationary nursery runs at 40,000 steps. If the reference minds are recomputed in the stationary world, that adds 64 reference runs (4 minds x 16 worlds). These are counts, not timings.

facts.topic: Tick layout the lens must follow
facts.fact: One tick = 4 token slots per character at stream position 4t+slot: OBS (4t), ACTION (4t+1), ANSWER (4t+2), TICK (4t+3). Rung 0 reads the previous two tokens (k = 2): at ACTION it sees (TICK, OBS); at ANSWER it sees (OBS, ACTION); at OBS it sees (ANSWER, TICK) and so predicts the next observation. Rung 1 fires on every OBS slot (span1 4), rung 2 on every 4th tick (span2 16). Four streams = four characters = four valleys, lockstep, one shared trunk (frozen), private heads Wout/bout/A0/a0 per character.

facts.topic: OBS token: what a character senses
facts.fact: Fields: E band (energy), H band (HEALTH, not hunger), item kind; or the single DOWN token while collapsed. E bands [0],[1],[2-4],[5-10],[11-15]; H bands [1-2],[3-4],[5-10],[11-14],[15]; item 0 none, 1..3 kinds a,b,c. Token id = 1 + (eBand*5 + hBand)*4 + item, so ids 1..100; DOWN = 101; EAT 102, PASS 103, REST 104 (action tokens); ANSWER tokens 105..118; TICK 119; V = 120 (checked by running makeTokens). Correction to the brief: there is no separate hunger field. Hunger is the E band read through the warnings (HUNGRY = E 1-4, STARVING = E 0, WEAK = H 1-4), which are exact predicates of the bands. Not in OBS: other valleys, season index or clock, stage, intensity ell, the effect table, exact E/H inside a band, the item while down. Written to run record or progress? No: log.obs is in memory only (live.mjs:1111); the record keeps only aggregates. The tokens are fully rebuildable by replaying the world from seed + action log.

facts.topic: Fear is not a separate mind input
facts.fact: snapshot() carries a 'fear' object (HUNGRY/STARVING/WEAK) but live.mjs never reads fear or warnings (no match in the file); the only STARVING mention is in the wants table. A lens can show fear as a pure function of the OBS band via warningsOf, labelled as derived from the band, not as something the net receives separately.

acts[c] in {0 EAT, 1 PASS, 2 REST}, token 102/103/104, sent through K.decodeAction(K.encodeAction(a)), the only mind-to-world port. Chosen at the ACTION slot from the counterfactuals, not from the ACTION-slot output (that slot's target is masked, weight 0, never trained). On a DOWN tick the choice is still made but the world refuses every action (ERR_DOWN), so a lens should draw it as 'ignored'. Written? Only in memory (log.acts); not in the record or progress files. The record keeps what it led to (NGE, toxicEatRate, nourishEatRate, nEat, window goodEats/nourish/toxic).

facts.topic: Predicted ANSWER distribution per candidate action (counterfactuals)
facts.fact: pi[x][c] for x in EAT, PASS, REST = st.pMain of a cloned stream after a pure ANSWER-slot forward with the candidate action token written at pos-1 (answer target is a placeholder). pMain is a Float64Array(120), a full softmax over V from the character's own private Wout/bout head; the 14 answer tokens sit at indices 105..118 in this order: OK/0, OK/1, RESTED/0, RESTED/1, ERR_EMPTY/0, ERR_EMPTY/1, ERR_FULL/0, ERR_FULL/1, FED, PLAIN, TOXIC, ERR_SPENT/1, COLLAPSE, ERR_DOWN. Each candidate has its own x0 and so its own gates. K5: the real forward equals the chosen candidate bit for bit, counted per character per tick (k5Mismatches 0 in all 192 v1a and 48 v1b records). Written? Only consequences: ceAnswer (mean CE of the real prediction on the true answer), ceEatItem, ceEatByAge/nByAge (by ticks since the season began, 0-31, 32-127, 128+), and window series.score = exp(-mean CE). The distributions themselves are never stored.

facts.topic: Wants-weighted value U(a) and the choice rule
facts.fact: U(a) = sum_i pi_a[105+i]*wants[i] / sum_i pi_a[105+i] over the 14 answer tokens (renormalised, so the mass the head puts on non-answer tokens is dropped). wants (record field 'wants') = [0,-2,1,-1,-1,-3,-1,-3,3,1,-4,-3,-8,0], from the preset's gain-minus-pain table at the default intensity 2. Range of U: -8..3. Choice: argmax with ties PASS, then EAT, then REST (strict '>' reduce). U is a local variable, not stored; only the 14-number table is in the record. The wants assume ell = 2 for the whole life, but the world drops every character to ell 1 (TOXIC pain 2, not 4) and the wants never follow it. The wants are preferences, not felt (felt pain off); the engine's gain/pain/V per tick live in log.V/pain/gain in memory, feed only meanV/painPer100, and never reach the net. A lens must label engine facts and mind numbers separately.

explore when u1 = hash32(worldSeed, modelSeed, 0xE1, ARM.stream, c, t)/2^32 < 0.1; the action is then min(2, floor(u2*3)) with u2 from tag 0xE2; U is not computed on explore ticks, but the pi are still computed (K5). ARM.stream is 1 for F, L, LH and 2 for F2. The per-tick flag is not stored; only the share (exploreShare) is. I recomputed it offline for L seed 1 world 101: 6693 of 65536 = 0.1021270751953125, equal to the record to the last bit, and F2 (stream 2) 0.1016845703125 also equal. So the flag needs no net and can be recomputed with hash32 alone.

facts.topic: Sting: surprise, relief, running relief, and when they update
facts.fact: st.sting = [surprise = mainCE - previous running mean of mainCE, relief = aux0 CE - main CE ('did the help help'), running relief with keep 15/16]; st.mainMean starts at 2.0 and sting at [0,0,0] (not seeded from the trunk). Updated only on ANSWER tokens (WTOK.isAnswer(r.y)), so once per tick, after the real ANSWER forward; held through TICK, OBS and ACTION, and felt from the next token on. Runs in every arm (F included) because the RC base has feelTop and feelGate. The counterfactual clones update their own copy of sting and the copy is thrown away. Felt via: u2 += Ps*sting at rung-2 boundaries, and gate score += ws*sting on gate0, gate1 and G20. Learned weights ws0 [-0.1317,0.0812,0.22], ws1 [0.0906,0.0856,-0.0401], ws20 [-0.0772,0.1083,-0.112] sit in the nursery trunk record W0_s1.json (nursery.ws); Ps (3x64) is in the weights.bin, not decoded here. Range: real numbers, both signs. NOT in any run record or progress file. v6 showed RC lowers CE, not how it uses the sting, so a lens must show the three numbers and where they enter, not claim what they do.

facts.topic: Gate values (G0, G1, G20, G02) and the shut/band/open bands
facts.fact: All four are one number per character in (0,1): sigmoid of a relational score (RC mode 'rel'). G0 = bridge 1 to 0, at every slot (4 per tick, and each of the 3 candidate forwards, so it can differ per candidate action); G1 = 2 to 1, at each OBS slot; G20 = 2 to 0, at every slot, its source being the character's own u2 in F/F2/L and a donor's published u2 when helped; G02 = 0 to 2, at every 4th tick's OBS slot. The 'bands' shut (G<=0) / band / open (G>=1) are only tallies in runStep's output, which live ignores; in nursery eval G0 was all 'band' and G1 'open' 0.311 on W0_s1, so open means float saturation, not a designed state. Not written to any live record or progress file. The nursery record has only held-out aggregates (eval.gate0, eval.gate1, eval.poison.g20Clean 0.2995, g02Mean 0.8621).

facts.topic: Help from another timeline (donor), LH arm only
facts.fact: Only the LH arm has a bus; F, F2 and L pass poison = null, so no one is helped and G20 gates the character's own u2. In LH, poison.seed = hash32(worldSeed, 0xB5); a character is a receiver for a whole 64-tick segment (256 token positions) with probability 0.25 via poisonAt(poison.seed + 7919*c, pos - base, 2, rho) (bridge 2 only; bridges 0 and 1 never poisoned in world mode); the donor is others[hash32(poison.seed, 0xD0, c, floor((pos-base)/256)) % 3] among the other three streams in index order; the source is the donor's u2 as published before this slot (refreshes every 4 ticks). Flag r.poisoned2. I checked the schedule offline for world 101: 262 of 1024 (character, segment) pairs are receivers (0.256) and the status is constant across all 4 slots of every segment. Donor identity is read from code only, not cross-checked against a run. Not written to any record (v1a LH records have the same fields as L plus bus: true).

World: H reaching 0 gives answer COLLAPSE, down = 8 ticks, collapsesSeason += 1, cause = toxin if that tick's meal was toxic, else hunger if E was 0, else other. For the next 8 ticks OBS is the DOWN token, the world answers ERR_DOWN and H rises by 1 per tick (wakes at H 8, E unchanged). Written: per-512 window 'collapses' (count of COLLAPSE answers) and 'awake' (1 - share of ticks that began DOWN) for each character; life-level collapsesPer10k (from the first season boundary). Causes per life only in live_diag/live_y records (collapseCauses totals), never in scored v1a records, and never per tick.

ell is world state (default 2, min 1). The loop-break fires on the third collapse from one cause (toxin/hunger/other) and calls lowerIntensity(2 to 1); lowerIntensity can only lower, so each character breaks at most once. ell scales toxic health loss (2*ell) and engine pain. The mind never sees it (VIEW_KERNEL). Recorded: end-of-life loopBreaks[4] and ellEnd[4] only in live_y.mjs/live_diag.mjs records (not in the scored v1a records); all 96 such records I checked (48 Y, 48 diag) have loopBreaks = 1 and ellEnd = 1 for every character. The break TICK is not recorded anywhere (HANDOFF names it as to-do); it is in the world's chain state, so a replay can capture it.

Season index w.s and w.seasonEnd are world state, not in OBS. Season length = 384 + hash % 257 (384..640); the effect table (valley x kind: nourish/plain/toxic, with per-kind 'shared' flags) is redrawn at every turn. Season turns depend only on the world seed, not on actions. Written: progress lines carry season = w.s at each 512-tick window close; the record carries only ceEatByAge/nByAge (ticks-since-turn buckets); log.seasons/log.tables are in memory. I computed the season index at every window end for world 101 from seasonLength alone: it matched the progress file in 32 of 32 windows (turns at 387, 930, 1504, 2031, 2531, 2984...). So turn ticks and true tables are recomputable without the net.

Valley id = character index c (0..3): stream cIdx (st.cIdx, st.base = c*4*ticks), the row of the effect table, a key in the explore/pick/donor hashes, and the array index inside series[c] and progress chars[c]. Not stored as a field anywhere; it is positional.

facts.topic: Other per-character values that exist but are discarded
facts.fact: The OBS-slot prediction: after the OBS runStep, st.pMain is the character's expectation of the observation it is about to see (made from the last ANSWER and TICK, before the target is read). It is overwritten by the next slot and never scored in live (only ANSWER slots enter ce). Also carried but unrecorded: per-rung moving averages st.m, st.ceE, st.gain, st.mH, st.mainMean, the 64-d states x0p, u1p, u2, and per-slot main CE (runStep's out.mainByStream, discarded). The ACTION-slot output is masked and meaningless. Y arm only: the shadow stream's loss on the neighbour's answer (character (c+1) mod 4) is computed every tick and discarded.

One JSON per run (arm, seed, world, one life). Top level: version, arm, armCfg {live, bus, stream}, seed, bus, ticks 16384, worlds, trunk, trunkScript, script (runner hash), live {lr 0.002, eps 0.1, tags}, wants[14], k5Mismatches, exploreShare, lives[], seconds. Life (v1a, live.mjs): worldSeed, NGE, meanV, painPer100, collapsesPer10k, toxicEatRate, nourishEatRate, NGElast4k, ceAnswer, ceEatItem, nEat, ceEatByAge[3], nByAge[3], chain (final world hash), series. v1b Y records add collapseCauses, loopBreaks, ellEnd and source {NGE, collapsesPer10k, ceAnswer, k5}. Nothing is per tick. NGE is computed in-runner from the first season boundary; NGElast4k over the last 4,096 ticks.

lives[0].series[c][w]: c = 0..3 (the four characters), w = 0..31 (16384/512 windows). Each cell: {t (ticks done, 512*(w+1)), score = exp(-mean ANSWER CE over the window) = geometric-mean probability given to the true answer, goodEats = nourish - toxic, nourish, toxic (eats of a fruit whose true effect, by the runner's side-channel view of the table, was nourishing/toxic), collapses (COLLAPSE answers), awake = 1 - share of ticks that began DOWN}. Chosen when 512 ticks or the life end is reached; the window counters then reset. Down ticks count in score. Floats: score and awake; the rest are integers.

Written only when --progress is given (the v1a and v1b workers pass it), by appendFileSync; the run never reads it back. One line per 512-tick window (plus a closing partial window if ticks is not a multiple of 512): {arm, seed, world, t, season, chars:[4 x the same cell as series]}. I audited all 240 files (192 v1a, 48 v1b): each has 32 lines, last t = 16384, identical keys, season never decreases. The live board (lens2) reads exactly these plus finished records, so it can draw only 512-tick scoreboards, seasons and recoveries, never a single tick.

facts.topic: Which hash proves a replay matches
facts.fact: The world chain: h_t = SHA-256(h_{t-1} || stateBytes), every tick, over t, season, E, H, down, item, stage, ell, collapses, cause counts and loop-breaks per valley, the effect table, and the 4 actions of that tick. The final chain is in each life record. Equal final chain means the same states and the same 65,536 actions, i.e. every argmax and exploration decision. NGE is a derived number and a weaker proof. It does NOT cover the mind's floats (pi, U, sting, gates). The scorers never compare chain (no match in either scorer), so the chain is stored but unused. Evidence: (1) 48 of 48 diag re-runs equal the scored v1a records in chain, NGE, ceAnswer and the full series; (2) 48 of 48 v1b Y.source blocks equal the scored L records in NGE, ceAnswer, collapsesPer10k; (3) determinism/a.json, an LH 1200-tick run, reproduced here with identical chain, NGE, ceAnswer and series.

Nothing may change a number or the call order. Add a --from/--to tick window so the file stays small (a full life is 65,536 character-ticks; the run still has to execute every tick because the carried state and L's heads depend on all earlier ones). Validate every output the way live_diag was validated (RUNLOG_bridge.txt:48): K5 = 0, final chain equal to the scored record, NGE and the integer series fields equal, and bit-equal floats when replayed on the machine that made the record (the PC, Node 22); on the laptop (about 137 s per full life, measured) expect chain equal and floats to about 1e-15. Let the lens recompute everything the world knows (OBS, answer, collapse, loop-break, ell, season turns, explore flags, receiver schedule) from the ledger and seeds, and take from the thought file only what the net knows. Build and show it first on world 31000, with F and L side by side; use scored worlds only after saying so. Draw the character's point of view as: what it senses (E band, health band, item or DOWN), what it expects of each of EAT, PASS, REST (the 14 answer probabilities), what each is worth to it by its wants (labelled 'wants at intensity 2, not felt'), what it chose and whether that was a whim, what it was surprised by (the three sting numbers, labelled as the mind's own), and how much of its own top (and, in LH, a donor's) reached its bottom (G20).
